The ANC - A House Divided

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The ANC finds itself at the head of crisis-ridden South Africa during a global pandemic. A state of emergency that has exposed deep divisions amid the systemic corruption that has ravaged the country.

Unique Selling Point:
This is a perilous time for South Africa. Mass unemployment and declining tax revenues are widening the scourge of inequality, even with heavy state borrowing. The ANC government is working on vaccinating enough people to reach herd immunity from the Covid-19 virus. Tragically, when the country is desperate for clear direction, divisions within the ANC are ever more apparent with widespread corruption and high profile cases coming to a head. President Ramaphosa is obfuscating, avoiding direct condemnation of former President Zuma’s defiance of the law. And, as a seasoned politician, he is looking after his own back by dithering over tackling the divisions that are splitting his party in two. There are so many senior figures in the ANC accused of corruption, they are almost powerless to expose each other, for fear of bringing the whole house down. At the very top of the ANC, defiant leaders and disdain for the rule of law has paralysed the ruling party, which begs the question, can the ANC and our democracy survive this factionalised leadership?

Summary:
Benevolence
The ANC, as the main liberation party in the long struggle of South Africans to break free from colonialism and apartheid, has a history of patronage. During the struggle people grew dependent on the organization for support throughout the decades of racial persecution. Customs that are ingrained in the ANC and ANC supporters that, as for most liberation movements, are hard to break when they get into government.

"Power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely"
In South Africa, the transition to government meant the ANC chose to make certain compromises. Some would regrettably provide opportunities for corrupt activities involving the pillaging of state coffers. Basic services were defined as commodities and the servicing of enterprises that provided them was commercialized. So that still, large state corporates are funded to deliver services countrywide while commercial companies are tendered to service those state owned enterprises. The means for stealing from the state was given by the patronage culture of the ruling ANC, providing networks through which bribes and sweeteners could determine the winners of contracts. And almost inevitably, these opportunities and means for defrauding the state provided the central motive for ‘state capture’, an operation for maximizing the loot and for helping the thieves get away with it.

But now, after years of escalating corruption, the state’s coffers are running dry, and with shortages made even more acute by the effect of the Covid-19 pandemic, finally corruption within the ANC has been identified as a critical challenge. The major complication to rooting out the culprits, is that the organization seen by many as best placed to take on the challenge is the ANC itself.

Further information:
We explore some of the examples of corruption that are under the spotlight that further threaten to destabilise the ANC and its position in eliminating patronage for the sake of honest governance. Can the ANC’s Integrity Commission ever be effective? The ANC are still apparently looking at the operation of the Integrity Commission - ANC asked Adv. Gcina Malidi for guidelines on how those implicated in corruption should be asked to step aside – the ANC also wants its own legal opinion on whether family members of ANC politicians should be barred from doing any business with the state.

Over the last 26 years we have heard many allegations of corruption within the government all involving multimillion rand deals that go astray. But when we look back, how many of the people who have been implicated have paid the price or been held accountable when facing the law? They can be counted on one hand. The very essence of the corruption and collusion to ensure that those implicated remained untouched, went as far as manipulation of prosecuting authorities. Former President Zuma’s defiance of the Concourt is part and parcel of this modus operandi and even the Secretary General of the ruling party concurs. So can the ANC hold some of its renegade members accountable and others not – and what does this mean for the prospects of the ANC bringing systemic corruption to an end… in reality, is the ANC anything but the best placed organization to take on the challenge, to save our democracy and the rule of law?

It is expected that the pivotal Top Six meeting with Zuma will take place either by the end of this week or next week (after postponement due to Zuma's Pietermaritzburg Court case). The outcome of this meeting will give a crucial signal regarding the political will of the ANC,
Will Zuma be compelled to testify or will he get arrested? And if the rule of law under properly appointed judges is followed under the auspices of the ANC it will be harder for Magashule to circumvent the law.


Example cases:

KZN Economic Development MEC, Mike Mabuyakhulo – one of the 16 accused of 2012 North Sea Jazz Festival which never took place – reinstated on recommendation of ANC’s KZN Integrity Commission despite the case still being ongoing (money laundering and corruption).

Setting of important precedent: Sacking of Eastern health care official – Oscar Mabuyane, Eastern Cape Premier fired Sindiswa Gomba, Eastern Cape Health MEC after charges against her relating to the Nelson Mandela funeral fraud case. Why did she get fired but Ace gets to choose? We have put in a request for an interview with Oscar Mabuyane.

ANC MP Bongani Bongo, former state security officer. The intertwining of Parliament and the courts, where the evidence leader of a parliamentary enquiry into Eskom reported Bongo for offering him a bribe to fake illness to avoid testifying at the enquiry and since he was evidence leader the inquiry would have to be halted. The case fell apart because of discrepancies between witness statements.


Contributors:

Steven Powell [ confirmed ]
Director: ENSafrica Forensics
Powell is testifying in the Zondo Commission on company employees collusion with government officials to secure tenders. He will not speak on his testimony as he still has to go back to the commission but we can use commission feed of it. Powell’s testimony is in regard to EOH and Geoff Makhubo, now the mayor Johannesburg. He can speak broadly on the way tenders can be used to bolster ANC coffers, eg during municipal elections.
Powell is now involved in anti-corruption compliance work, putting programs in place in corporates to prevent corruption. In this role he has seen lots more of what goes wrong and can speak on this and on anti-corruption guidelines.

Professor William Gumede [ confirmed ]
Associate Professor, School of Governance at the University of the Witwatersrand and Executive Chairperson of Democracy Works.
Gumede has researched the ANC and its history, amongst other African liberation movements. His general take is that one of the reasons we're in this dire situation is that the ANC has always been a very broad church without anything really holding it together. The only thing that did was the fight against apartheid. Now, in government, the party needs some kind of common consensus around policy and focus around the diversity of policies. This is absent, so in Gumede's view, almost the only way out for the ANC and for South Africa is for the ANC to break up and come up with a new political party, like has happened elsewhere in Africa.

Judith February [ confirmed ]
Lawyer, governance specialist and columnist
February's areas of focus include corruption and its impact on governance, Parliamentary oversight and institutional design.
On Zuma defying the Zondo commission, February has said "The president missed an opportunity to put his head above the parapet and speak, as head of state, in defence of the Constitution. That was another example of Ramaphosa taking the easy way out and trying not to offend any of his corrupt comrades within the ANC."

Former President Kgalema Motlanthe [ awaiting confirmation ]
As a veteran of the ANC Motlanthe can perhaps add a more elevated ANC perspective. He is interesting in that he was considered a caretaker President for Zuma, is regarded as a ‘the ANC comes first’ man and reportedly was and is committed to the notion that strict accountability by ANC officials must be followed. So what has Motlanthe to say about the current shenanigans and what must be done about them?

Oscar Mabuyane Eastern Cape Premier [ Request made ]

George Mashamba, ANC Integrity Commission [ requested interview through Pule Mabe who is not picking up phone - Mashamba's number straight to voice mail ]

Press Release:


A house divided will not stand. In an effort to clean up corruption, the ANC risks bringing the edifice down with it, in a bitter fight for control.
At the very top of the ANC, defiant leaders and disdain for the rule of law has paralysed the party. Can our democracy survive this fractured leadership?


Script:


VO: In 26 years of South African democracy only one party has held the reins of power, the African National Congress. A global pandemic and a state of disaster have exposed deep divisions within the ANC and the systemic corruption that is ravaging the country./ /
Senior member of the National Executive Committee of the ANC, and former Deputy Minister of Finance Mondli Gungubele, believes the party is at a crossroads.

Mondli: If you read the letter of the President and look at the resolutions of the conference, Our renewal position in 2017 does reach that point that ANC is viewed as being the main character in corruption.

VO: But the organization seen by many as best placed to take on the challenge, is the ANC itself.

Mondli: An ANC that is dubious with regard to the issues of corruption, especially as they affect the ANC itself, is actually in my view putting this country in danger because to me, ANC is central to the stability of this country It is central to the prosperity of this country.

VO: According to political scientist and author of the Battle for the Soul of the ANC, Professor William Gumede, the schism within the party is rooted in an historical system of patronage.

William Gumede: So, there are two factions in the ANC essentially, two bigger factions. So one faction one could say is a Cyril Ramaphosa faction, the other faction is led by Ace Magashule and Jacob Zuma. And they are not factions based on ideology and on policy, they're really factions based on control of resources.
Bongani Bingwa [01:47]
You coined the phrase, the battle for the soul of the ANC. It's meant different things in different eras of the organisation, hasn't it?
William Gumede: When the ANC was a liberation movement, it was almost like a broad church where the party became a patronage party, even in exile, and, and becoming a patronage Party actually made them effective, in the struggle against apartheid. The party itself became almost also a parallel administration where you gave jobs to loyal people, and if you’re disloyal, you're not going to get a job. Then the party came to power in 1994 and it moved their patronage system onto the state, it grafted it onto the state.

VO: Basic services were defined as commodities and the servicing of enterprises that provided them was commercialized. Inadvertently, these opportunities designed for economic transformation became a means for unscrupulous actors to defraud the state through ANC networks.

William Gumede: And now what we have is just a bitter fight for control over resources.

LINK: Luthuli house at the corner of Helen Joseph and Pixley Ka Seme, an edifice to a glorious movement that is now tearing itself apart and taking the country down with it.

Mondli: Any sense of instability in our party doesn't send a good message for the country. But in the manner some of our comrades conduct themselves, it is shocking and disappointing. And I dare say, unless the organisation deals with it, at some stage we will have to live with the consequences.

VO: Consequences that will affect every citizen. Analyst and governance specialist Judith February maintains that the divide between the ANC camps is irreconcilable.

Judith: Those who are earnest about doing good for the country, and those who believe in the Constitution, and then others who are frankly, like former President Jacob Zuma constitutional vandals, and they will do anything in their power to take the edifice down with them, and in their own interests.

William Gumede: If the ANC was really serious about corruption and about accountability, he would have been suspended as a member of the ANC. So if they take him on, the fear is that his supporters will then fight back in the ANC.

Upsound: Presidente….chanting
VO: The main face of this fight, and poised as a contender for the presidency, is the Secretary General, Ace Magashule, who is currently facing 21 charges of corruption.

Mondli: How we are handling the SG's matter, unintentionally, it sends a message to the public that we are weak, that we are at his mercy which doesn't speak well about the organisation. it doesn't speak well about our decisiveness.
Bongani Bingwa: It doesn't suggest you are decisive on Magashule, or on the former President Zuma.
Mondli: I agree.

LINK: In an effort to clean up, the National Executive Committee of the ANC, the Party's highest decision making body between conferences is grappling with processes to deal with members who are either criminally charged or accused of wrongdoing.

VO: The NEC is awaiting further guidance from top officials on implementing the 2017 Nasrec ‘step aside’ resolution. But already, in December last year the ANC’s Integrity Commission recommended that the Secretary General himself relinquish his post.

Mondli: The resolutions of the conference are very clear in directing all of us to comply with the law enforcement agents. I say he has been reckless, to me, he has acted like a rogue element. He has showed the Constitution of the organisation and his resolution, a middle finger in public more than two times.

William Gumede: So he is now, he’s in a faceoff with Ramaphosa. If Ace magashule wins I think what he will do he will then feel that he's strengthened enough to topple Cyril Ramaphosa.
Bongani Bingwa: Can he do it? Can Ace become president ?
William Gumede: If he wins on this guideline, his strength would be to such an extent that he can do that. So that is why it is so important for Cyril Ramaphosa to enforce this guideline and force him to step down

VO: But there are many ANC leaders embroiled in corruption allegations, with an apparent reluctance to hold them accountable for fear of bringing the whole house down. And many will argue, what has happened to innocent until proven guilty?

Mondli: The resolution says, to protect the image of the organisation during the period of your case, don't make the organisation find itself spread, dealing with the prosecution of its programme and explaining you, whilst the big mission of the organisation is about the nation as a whole.

VO: Whilst some members defy the resolutions others are making an example of them. In February Eastern Cape Premier Oscar Mabuyane fired the MEC for Health Sindiswa Gomba, after she refused to step aside while facing charges for misappropriating funds earmarked for Nelson Mandela’s funeral in 2013.
Oscar Mabuyane.. ECPG PRESS CONFERENCE Feb 18 2021

VO: In the meantime the jury's still out on whether the ANC top six will manage to convince the former president to appear before the commission into State Capture. If not, Zuma could face a two year jail sentence.

William Gumede: It appears that he and other senior ANC leaders are above the law. Now, once you have one group of citizens above the law, the others sort of low level people with no networks, not in the party, they can get prosecuted. We then have no constitutional democracy anymore. So if the ANC says it wants to hold people accountable, the very first person that it needs to hold accountable is Jacob Zuma.

VO: This disobedience for the rule of law threatens to derail the inquiry into state capture. Auswell Mashaba, former head of Swifambo, a PRASA supplier, took his lead from Jacob Zuma and defied a summons to appear before the Commission.

Auswell Mashaba / State Capture Inquiry The Commission hears PRASA related evidence Ryan Marc Sacks.mp4 [00:38:14 ]
Zondo: This conduct by anybody, if it spreads it will be the beginning of chaos in our legal system.

VO: It is a mistake to think that this corruption is only about individuals as some of the information emerging from the State Capture commission suggests the ANC party itself stood to benefit either directly or indirectly.
(images of PRASA and EOH at Zondo)

William Gumede: So the moment one gets to a position,which has been the case where you get a state contract, and part of that contract, almost a percentage has to go to the ANC. And it's not only at the national level, but it also happened at the municipal level, that a cut goes to the local ANC ;to the local party. It is very difficult to, you know, to eradicate that culture.

VO: There is a narrative that seeks to blame all of the country's woes on the Zuma years. And yet, the endemic culture of corruption within the ANC didn't begin or end with Zuma

Bongani Bingwa: Aren't we here, ultimately, because the party has placed its unity above the interests of the country?
Mondli: I think there's a deliberate exercise by criminals in the organisation to misuse the word unity, to defend malfeasance, which are very detrimental to the image of this organisation, which is so central to the believability of this country, to the investor community to all South Africans, who must actually see their future in this country.
Bongani Bingwa: Is it inevitable that there will be two ANCs? The organisation will split?
Mondli: I wish that doesn't happen Bongani. But if it is a split between the cadres of the movements who want to run a noble ANC and criminals who are corrupt, so be it.

Holywell_Walker_Kelly UPM_CHAP527 TX Details Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 07 March 2021 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 23 February 2022 Press Release: A house divided will not stand. In an effort to clean up corruption, the ANC risks bringing the edifice down with it, in a bitter fight for control. At the very top of the ANC, defiant leaders and disdain for the rule of law has paralysed the party. Can our democracy survive this fractured leadership? Script: VO: In 26 years of South African democracy only one party has held the reins of power, the African National Congress. A global pandemic and a state of disaster have exposed deep divisions within the ANC and the systemic corruption that is ravaging the country./ / Senior member of the National Executive Committee of the ANC, and former Deputy Minister of Finance Mondli Gungubele, believes the party is at a crossroads. Mondli: If you read the letter of the President and look at the resolutions of the conference, Our renewal position in 2017 does reach that point that ANC is viewed as being the main character in corruption. VO: But the organization seen by many as best placed to take on the challenge, is the ANC itself. Mondli: An ANC that is dubious with regard to the issues of corruption, especially as they affect the ANC itself, is actually in my view putting this country in danger because to me, ANC is central to the stability of this country It is central to the prosperity of this country. VO: According to political scientist and author of the Battle for the Soul of the ANC, Professor William Gumede, the schism within the party is rooted in an historical system of patronage. William Gumede: So, there are two factions in the ANC essentially, two bigger factions. So one faction one could say is a Cyril Ramaphosa faction, the other faction is led by Ace Magashule and Jacob Zuma. And they are not factions based on ideology and on policy, they're really factions based on control of resources. Bongani Bingwa [01:47] You coined the phrase, the battle for the soul of the ANC. It's meant different things in different eras of the organisation, hasn't it? William Gumede: When the ANC was a liberation movement, it was almost like a broad church where the party became a patronage party, even in exile, and, and becoming a patronage Party actually made them effective, in the struggle against apartheid. The party itself became almost also a parallel administration where you gave jobs to loyal people, and if you’re disloyal, you're not going to get a job. Then the party came to power in 1994 and it moved their patronage system onto the state, it grafted it onto the state. VO: Basic services were defined as commodities and the servicing of enterprises that provided them was commercialized. Inadvertently, these opportunities designed for economic transformation became a means for unscrupulous actors to defraud the state through ANC networks. William Gumede: And now what we have is just a bitter fight for control over resources. LINK: Luthuli house at the corner of Helen Joseph and Pixley Ka Seme, an edifice to a glorious movement that is now tearing itself apart and taking the country down with it. Mondli: Any sense of instability in our party doesn't send a good message for the country. But in the manner some of our comrades conduct themselves, it is shocking and disappointing. And I dare say, unless the organisation deals with it, at some stage we will have to live with the consequences. VO: Consequences that will affect every citizen. Analyst and governance specialist Judith February maintains that the divide between the ANC camps is irreconcilable. Judith: Those who are earnest about doing good for the country, and those who believe in the Constitution, and then others who are frankly, like former President Jacob Zuma constitutional vandals, and they will do anything in their power to take the edifice down with them, and in their own interests. William Gumede: If the ANC was really serious about corruption and about accountability, he would have been suspended as a member of the ANC. So if they take him on, the fear is that his supporters will then fight back in the ANC. Upsound: Presidente….chanting VO: The main face of this fight, and poised as a contender for the presidency, is the Secretary General, Ace Magashule, who is currently facing 21 charges of corruption. Mondli: How we are handling the SG's matter, unintentionally, it sends a message to the public that we are weak, that we are at his mercy which doesn't speak well about the organisation. it doesn't speak well about our decisiveness. Bongani Bingwa: It doesn't suggest you are decisive on Magashule, or on the former President Zuma. Mondli: I agree. LINK: In an effort to clean up, the National Executive Committee of the ANC, the Party's highest decision making body between conferences is grappling with processes to deal with members who are either criminally charged or accused of wrongdoing. VO: The NEC is awaiting further guidance from top officials on implementing the 2017 Nasrec ‘step aside’ resolution. But already, in December last year the ANC’s Integrity Commission recommended that the Secretary General himself relinquish his post. Mondli: The resolutions of the conference are very clear in directing all of us to comply with the law enforcement agents. I say he has been reckless, to me, he has acted like a rogue element. He has showed the Constitution of the organisation and his resolution, a middle finger in public more than two times. William Gumede: So he is now, he’s in a faceoff with Ramaphosa. If Ace magashule wins I think what he will do he will then feel that he's strengthened enough to topple Cyril Ramaphosa. Bongani Bingwa: Can he do it? Can Ace become president ? William Gumede: If he wins on this guideline, his strength would be to such an extent that he can do that. So that is why it is so important for Cyril Ramaphosa to enforce this guideline and force him to step down VO: But there are many ANC leaders embroiled in corruption allegations, with an apparent reluctance to hold them accountable for fear of bringing the whole house down. And many will argue, what has happened to innocent until proven guilty? Mondli: The resolution says, to protect the image of the organisation during the period of your case, don't make the organisation find itself spread, dealing with the prosecution of its programme and explaining you, whilst the big mission of the organisation is about the nation as a whole. VO: Whilst some members defy the resolutions others are making an example of them. In February Eastern Cape Premier Oscar Mabuyane fired the MEC for Health Sindiswa Gomba, after she refused to step aside while facing charges for misappropriating funds earmarked for Nelson Mandela’s funeral in 2013. Oscar Mabuyane.. ECPG PRESS CONFERENCE Feb 18 2021 VO: In the meantime the jury's still out on whether the ANC top six will manage to convince the former president to appear before the commission into State Capture. If not, Zuma could face a two year jail sentence. William Gumede: It appears that he and other senior ANC leaders are above the law. Now, once you have one group of citizens above the law, the others sort of low level people with no networks, not in the party, they can get prosecuted. We then have no constitutional democracy anymore. So if the ANC says it wants to hold people accountable, the very first person that it needs to hold accountable is Jacob Zuma. VO: This disobedience for the rule of law threatens to derail the inquiry into state capture. Auswell Mashaba, former head of Swifambo, a PRASA supplier, took his lead from Jacob Zuma and defied a summons to appear before the Commission. Auswell Mashaba / State Capture Inquiry The Commission hears PRASA related evidence Ryan Marc Sacks.mp4 [00:38:14 ] Zondo: This conduct by anybody, if it spreads it will be the beginning of chaos in our legal system. VO: It is a mistake to think that this corruption is only about individuals as some of the information emerging from the State Capture commission suggests the ANC party itself stood to benefit either directly or indirectly. (images of PRASA and EOH at Zondo) William Gumede: So the moment one gets to a position,which has been the case where you get a state contract, and part of that contract, almost a percentage has to go to the ANC. And it's not only at the national level, but it also happened at the municipal level, that a cut goes to the local ANC ;to the local party. It is very difficult to, you know, to eradicate that culture. VO: There is a narrative that seeks to blame all of the country's woes on the Zuma years. And yet, the endemic culture of corruption within the ANC didn't begin or end with Zuma Bongani Bingwa: Aren't we here, ultimately, because the party has placed its unity above the interests of the country? Mondli: I think there's a deliberate exercise by criminals in the organisation to misuse the word unity, to defend malfeasance, which are very detrimental to the image of this organisation, which is so central to the believability of this country, to the investor community to all South Africans, who must actually see their future in this country. Bongani Bingwa: Is it inevitable that there will be two ANCs? The organisation will split? Mondli: I wish that doesn't happen Bongani. But if it is a split between the cadres of the movements who want to run a noble ANC and criminals who are corrupt, so be it.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The ANC finds itself at the head of crisis-ridden South Africa during a global pandemic. A state of emergency that has exposed deep divisions amid the systemic corruption that has ravaged the country.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: This is a perilous time for South Africa. Mass unemployment and declining tax revenues are widening the scourge of inequality, even with heavy state borrowing. The ANC government is working on vaccinating enough people to reach herd immunity from the Covid-19 virus. Tragically, when the country is desperate for clear direction, divisions within the ANC are ever more apparent with widespread corruption and high profile cases coming to a head. President Ramaphosa is obfuscating, avoiding direct condemnation of former President Zuma’s defiance of the law. And, as a seasoned politician, he is looking after his own back by dithering over tackling the divisions that are splitting his party in two. There are so many senior figures in the ANC accused of corruption, they are almost powerless to expose each other, for fear of bringing the whole house down. At the very top of the ANC, defiant leaders and disdain for the rule of law has paralysed the ruling party, which begs the question, can the ANC and our democracy survive this factionalised leadership?
metadata.Summary: Benevolence The ANC, as the main liberation party in the long struggle of South Africans to break free from colonialism and apartheid, has a history of patronage. During the struggle people grew dependent on the organization for support throughout the decades of racial persecution. Customs that are ingrained in the ANC and ANC supporters that, as for most liberation movements, are hard to break when they get into government. "Power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely" In South Africa, the transition to government meant the ANC chose to make certain compromises. Some would regrettably provide opportunities for corrupt activities involving the pillaging of state coffers. Basic services were defined as commodities and the servicing of enterprises that provided them was commercialized. So that still, large state corporates are funded to deliver services countrywide while commercial companies are tendered to service those state owned enterprises. The means for stealing from the state was given by the patronage culture of the ruling ANC, providing networks through which bribes and sweeteners could determine the winners of contracts. And almost inevitably, these opportunities and means for defrauding the state provided the central motive for ‘state capture’, an operation for maximizing the loot and for helping the thieves get away with it. But now, after years of escalating corruption, the state’s coffers are running dry, and with shortages made even more acute by the effect of the Covid-19 pandemic, finally corruption within the ANC has been identified as a critical challenge. The major complication to rooting out the culprits, is that the organization seen by many as best placed to take on the challenge is the ANC itself.
metadata.Further information: We explore some of the examples of corruption that are under the spotlight that further threaten to destabilise the ANC and its position in eliminating patronage for the sake of honest governance. Can the ANC’s Integrity Commission ever be effective? The ANC are still apparently looking at the operation of the Integrity Commission - ANC asked Adv. Gcina Malidi for guidelines on how those implicated in corruption should be asked to step aside – the ANC also wants its own legal opinion on whether family members of ANC politicians should be barred from doing any business with the state. Over the last 26 years we have heard many allegations of corruption within the government all involving multimillion rand deals that go astray. But when we look back, how many of the people who have been implicated have paid the price or been held accountable when facing the law? They can be counted on one hand. The very essence of the corruption and collusion to ensure that those implicated remained untouched, went as far as manipulation of prosecuting authorities. Former President Zuma’s defiance of the Concourt is part and parcel of this modus operandi and even the Secretary General of the ruling party concurs. So can the ANC hold some of its renegade members accountable and others not – and what does this mean for the prospects of the ANC bringing systemic corruption to an end… in reality, is the ANC anything but the best placed organization to take on the challenge, to save our democracy and the rule of law? It is expected that the pivotal Top Six meeting with Zuma will take place either by the end of this week or next week (after postponement due to Zuma's Pietermaritzburg Court case). The outcome of this meeting will give a crucial signal regarding the political will of the ANC, Will Zuma be compelled to testify or will he get arrested? And if the rule of law under properly appointed judges is followed under the auspices of the ANC it will be harder for Magashule to circumvent the law. Example cases: KZN Economic Development MEC, Mike Mabuyakhulo – one of the 16 accused of 2012 North Sea Jazz Festival which never took place – reinstated on recommendation of ANC’s KZN Integrity Commission despite the case still being ongoing (money laundering and corruption). Setting of important precedent: Sacking of Eastern health care official – Oscar Mabuyane, Eastern Cape Premier fired Sindiswa Gomba, Eastern Cape Health MEC after charges against her relating to the Nelson Mandela funeral fraud case. Why did she get fired but Ace gets to choose? We have put in a request for an interview with Oscar Mabuyane. ANC MP Bongani Bongo, former state security officer. The intertwining of Parliament and the courts, where the evidence leader of a parliamentary enquiry into Eskom reported Bongo for offering him a bribe to fake illness to avoid testifying at the enquiry and since he was evidence leader the inquiry would have to be halted. The case fell apart because of discrepancies between witness statements. Contributors: Steven Powell [ confirmed ] Director: ENSafrica Forensics Powell is testifying in the Zondo Commission on company employees collusion with government officials to secure tenders. He will not speak on his testimony as he still has to go back to the commission but we can use commission feed of it. Powell’s testimony is in regard to EOH and Geoff Makhubo, now the mayor Johannesburg. He can speak broadly on the way tenders can be used to bolster ANC coffers, eg during municipal elections. Powell is now involved in anti-corruption compliance work, putting programs in place in corporates to prevent corruption. In this role he has seen lots more of what goes wrong and can speak on this and on anti-corruption guidelines. Professor William Gumede [ confirmed ] Associate Professor, School of Governance at the University of the Witwatersrand and Executive Chairperson of Democracy Works. Gumede has researched the ANC and its history, amongst other African liberation movements. His general take is that one of the reasons we're in this dire situation is that the ANC has always been a very broad church without anything really holding it together. The only thing that did was the fight against apartheid. Now, in government, the party needs some kind of common consensus around policy and focus around the diversity of policies. This is absent, so in Gumede's view, almost the only way out for the ANC and for South Africa is for the ANC to break up and come up with a new political party, like has happened elsewhere in Africa. Judith February [ confirmed ] Lawyer, governance specialist and columnist February's areas of focus include corruption and its impact on governance, Parliamentary oversight and institutional design. On Zuma defying the Zondo commission, February has said "The president missed an opportunity to put his head above the parapet and speak, as head of state, in defence of the Constitution. That was another example of Ramaphosa taking the easy way out and trying not to offend any of his corrupt comrades within the ANC." Former President Kgalema Motlanthe [ awaiting confirmation ] As a veteran of the ANC Motlanthe can perhaps add a more elevated ANC perspective. He is interesting in that he was considered a caretaker President for Zuma, is regarded as a ‘the ANC comes first’ man and reportedly was and is committed to the notion that strict accountability by ANC officials must be followed. So what has Motlanthe to say about the current shenanigans and what must be done about them? Oscar Mabuyane Eastern Cape Premier [ Request made ] George Mashamba, ANC Integrity Commission [ requested interview through Pule Mabe who is not picking up phone - Mashamba's number straight to voice mail ]
